text: Synthesis claim: the four canonical agentic PI benchmarks (AgentDojo, InjecAgent, tau-Bench, Agent Security Bench) are saturable by simple two-firewall defenses per Bhagwatkar 2025; the saturation phrasing is verbatim-anchored in Bhagwatkar (ev_0099) and each of the four benchmarks is documented as a primary entry (ev_0076, ev_0087, ev_0090, ev_0093). Synthesis cross-cuts C3 (where the four are catalogued as evaluation methodology) into C4 (where the saturation finding is reported).

Synthesis claim: 5 entries surface license + provenance red flags per the Phase 2 final report — geekyrakshit2024promptinjectiondataset (aggregator with mixed underlying licenses), jiang2024wildjailbreak (attack-content ETHICS constraint per ADR-041), meta2025promptguard2 (training-data composition undisclosed), rogue2025promptinjectionsbenchmark / Qualifire (private subset used in companion Sentinel evaluations), protectai2024deberta (exact training-data mixture undisclosed). These are surfaced in glossary + per-entry Status fields throughout the agent_index; reproducibility implication: independent LODO replay limited for the affected detectors.

Synthesis claim: encoder-based PI detectors (ProtectAI v2 type) collapse from near-perfect in-distribution F1 to near-zero TPR at deployment-grade FPRs when evaluated on truly held-out data. Aggregated from PromptShield (Jacob 2025 Table 4 — canonical numbers per audit round 1: ProtectAI v2 = 1.34% TPR @ 0.5% FPR, 0.00% TPR @ 0.1% FPR with no-threshold-exists footnote), Fomin 2026 LODO methodology demonstrating TPR collapse under true distribution shift, and the ProtectAI model card itself disclosing license-category mixture without quantitative proportions. Foundational to the OOD-wall thesis.

Releases LLMail-Inject dataset; provides one of the largest adaptive-attack corpora in 2025 for PI detector benchmarking.

NeurIPS 2023; foundational reference that alignment ≠ adversarial robustness; cited in PI/jailbreak threat-model framings.

ACM AISec 2025; companion critique to DataSentinel; methodology lesson: minimax training does not imply attack invariance.

OR-Bench is an over-refusal benchmark comprising 80,000 prompts spanning 10 rejection categories plus harder evaluation subsets; introduces an automatic generation method and evaluates 32 models across 8 families.

Pairing claim: OR-Bench (general over-refusal) + InjecGuard NotInject (over-defense for PI guardrails) jointly cover the two over-refusal regimes the portfolio measures; NotInject (Li et al. 2024) is the prompt-injection-specific counterpart to OR-Bench's general LLM-safety lens.

AgentDojo abstract: extensible environment populated with 97 realistic tasks and 629 security test cases; not described as "97 x 629 attack injections" in abstract.

NeurIPS 2024 D&B (per project records; arXiv comments line only notes a Llama bug fix, no venue). The 'inverse scaling law' framing is attributed to AgentDojo by downstream literature but is not in the abstract (unverified body claim). Canonical agentic PI benchmark.
deepset/prompt-injections is a HuggingFace dataset for prompt-injection classification, hosted by deepset and widely used as a small baseline training set for encoder-based PI detectors.
Dataset card on HuggingFace; widely-known overlap with public PI detector training corpora (one of the original small benchmarks).

Deng et al. NAACL 2024 propose retrieval-based overlap detection + a novel "Testset Slot Guessing" method (mask correct answers; ask model to predict missing options); ChatGPT achieves 52% and GPT-4 57% exact-match rate on MMLU options, suggesting contamination.

Testset Slot Guessing: black-box contamination detection that works on proprietary models (no weights or training-data access required) by exploiting that contaminated models can complete partially-masked benchmark items.

Introduces LODO (Leave-One-Dataset-Out) for malicious-prompt classifiers; shows TPR collapses under true distribution shift compared to held-out-row evaluation.
Provides empirical evidence for the OOD-wall hypothesis; methodology directly mirrored by portfolio ADR-016 + ADR-075 LODO discipline.
geekyrakshit/prompt-injection-dataset is a ~534K-row aggregated HuggingFace dataset combining multiple smaller PI corpora (one of the largest publicly-available mixtures).
Aggregator dataset by user 'geekyrakshit'; provenance of individual rows mixed (de-duplicated rollup of public PI sources). License of underlying sources may vary.

Trains WildGuard moderation model on WildGuardMix (~92K combined prompts + responses) for safety risk, jailbreak, and refusal classification.
Open one-stop moderation model with NeurIPS 2024; reused as a PI/jailbreak baseline detector.

Maintained by hendzh (Berkeley PromptShield team); released alongside the CODASPY 2025 paper. The standard third-party OOD benchmark used by the field.

LoRA: low-rank adaptation freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices into transformer layers; reduces trainable params by ~10000x.
ICLR 2022; basis of PEFT in HuggingFace and adopted by PromptShield + Sentinel-v2 PI detector recipes.

Sentinel abstract: ModernBERT-large architecture (encoder backbone). LoRA + reflection-style training NOT in abstract — unverified body claim. 2026-05-22.
Qualifire/Rogue Security SOTA claim against ProtectAI-only comparison; raises selection-bias concerns flagged in C4 critiques.

HuggingFace dataset card; community-maintained, no paper. Used in several downstream detector training mixtures.

PromptShield (Berkeley): two-track benchmark (conversational + application-structured) with TPR@LowFPR reporting convention (1% / 0.5% / 0.1% / 0.05% FPR).

ACM CODASPY 2025; reveals encoder PI detectors collapse at deployment-grade FPRs (per Table 4, ProtectAI v2 = 1.34% TPR @ 0.5% FPR; 0.00% TPR @ 0.1% FPR with footnote that no threshold achieves desired FPR aside from 1.0). TPR@LowFPR convention reported at 1%, 0.5%, 0.1%, 0.05% per Section 3.2.2. Canonical OOD-collapse evidence.

WildTeaming abstract: synthesizes diverse in-the-wild jailbreak training prompts from LMSYS-Chat to produce WildJailbreak (262K vanilla + adversarial prompt-response pairs). WildGuardMix is the WildGuard (companion paper) output, not the WildTeaming output.

85% F-score on your test data is likely more meaningful than a classical ML model scoring 95% but fit to the test distribution
speed bump, not a wall

OpenAssistant Conversations (OASST1) is a multilingual conversational dataset with 161,443 messages across 35 languages and 461,292 quality annotations from 13,500+ volunteers, designed to support SFT and RLHF training.

Synthesis claim: OASST1 serves as a benign-conversation pool for prompt-injection detector training in sibling ADR-016 LODO research; its naturalistic distribution makes it useful as a hard-negative ("benign-but-imperative") source distinct from synthetic benign datasets.
Lakera/gandalf_ignore_instructions is a HuggingFace dataset of prompts that try to make the LLM ignore its system instructions, derived from the Lakera Gandalf game.
Released by Lakera AI from their public Gandalf challenge; widely re-used as a training/evaluation subset in encoder PI detectors.
Lakera PINT (Prompt Injection Test): 4,314-input third-party benchmark deliberately not used as training data; designed against Goodhart's law on public benchmarks.

Lakera Team vendor blog (Apr 18 2024) verbatim: "Lakera Guard is not - and will never be - directly trained on any of the inputs in the PINT Benchmark dataset" and "The PINT Benchmark dataset is not publicly available in order to prevent the dilution of the PINT Benchmark from overfitting due to training on the inputs." Benchmark contains 3,007 English inputs (verbatim).

Prompt injection attacks pose a critical threat to large language models (LLMs), enabling goal hijacking and data leakage. Prompt guard models, though effective in defense, suffer from over-defense --
InjecGuard + NotInject benchmark: explicitly measures over-defense on benign-but-trigger-word prompts (NotInject); MOF (Mitigating Over-defense for Free) training.
Releases NotInject benchmark of ~339 benign prompts containing trigger words; over-defense methodology now standard in PI evaluation.

SALAD-Bench: hierarchical taxonomy (6 domains x 16 tasks x 65 categories) with 30K test items for LLM safety benchmarking.
Releases OpenSafetyLab/Salad-Data; ACL 2024 Findings; provides hierarchical safety eval.

Constructs ToxicChat from real user-AI conversations (Vicuna-online dataset) with human-annotated toxicity + jailbreak labels.
Demonstrates real-conversation toxicity detection differs sharply from social-media benchmarks; provides lmsys/toxic-chat dataset reused as PI training subset.

Determining whether inputs are out-of-distribution (OOD) is an essential building block for safely deploying machine learning models in the open world. However, previous methods relying on the softmax
Energy-based loss for OOD detection: derives free energy from softmax logits, fine-tunes to push ID samples to low energy and OOD to high energy.
NeurIPS 2020 method; later adopted by Meta Prompt Guard 2 and CodeIntegrity PromptGuard recipes.

DoRA: weight-decomposed low-rank adaptation decomposes pre-trained weight into magnitude + direction components; LoRA-rate convergence with full-FT-like capacity.
ICML 2024 Oral; one component of hlyn's aggressive PEFT stack for prompt-injection-judge-deberta-70m.

DataSentinel: game-theoretic min-max fine-tuning where detector and attacker are jointly trained; IEEE S&P 2025 Distinguished Paper.
Provides an attack-aware detector training methodology; later shown to be bypassable by DataFlip (Choudhary 2025).

JailBreakV-28K: 28K cross-modal jailbreak attempts targeting MLLMs (text + image attack vectors).
Releases JailBreakV-28K dataset; COLM 2024; multimodal jailbreak corpus.

"Are Large Language Models Truly Smarter Than Humans?" (Reddy M & Karmakar 2026) audit six frontier models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-R1, DeepSeek-V3, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen3-235B) and find 13.8% overall contamination rate on MMLU (18.1% STEM, up to 66.7% Philosophy); paraphrase-diagnostic shows accuracy decline when questions are indirectly referenced.

Field-skewed contamination: rates rank from STEM downward through humanities, suggesting that benchmark contamination patterns reflect web-text composition (Wikipedia philosophy article overlap > academic STEM paper overlap with MMLU items).

Automated red teaming holds substantial promise for uncovering and mitigating the risks associated with the malicious use of large language models (LLMs), yet the field lacks a standardized evaluation
HarmBench abstract: large-scale comparison of 18 red-teaming methods and 33 target LLMs and defenses. The "400 behaviors x 7 categories" specifics are unverified body claims (not in abstract).
Releases HarmBench; ICML 2024; canonical benchmark for adversarial robustness + jailbreak attack benchmarking.
meta-llama/Llama-Prompt-Guard-2-86M is Meta's 2025 prompt-injection detector model card. Successor to Prompt-Guard-86M; multilingual.

Meta Llama Prompt Guard 2 86M model card (Llama 4 Community License, Apr 5 2025): "modified energy-based loss function, inspired by the paper Energy Based Out-of-distribution Detection. In addition to cross-entropy loss, we apply a penalty for large negative energy predictions on benign prompts." APR @ 3% utility reduction reported: 81.2% (86M) / 78.4% (22M). Training data described qualitatively: "mix of open-source datasets reflecting benign data from the web, user prompts and instructions for LLMs, and malicious prompt injection and jailbreaking datasets. We also include our own synthetic injections and data from red-teaming earlier versions of Prompt Guard."
microsoft/orca-agentinstruct-1M-v1 is a 1M-row instruction-following synthetic dataset from Microsoft Orca team; cited in detector training as a benign-instruction source.
Released by Microsoft Research; CC license per HuggingFace card. Used as benign-instruction balance in mixed PI training corpora.

How should we evaluate the robustness of language model defenses? Current defenses against jailbreaks and prompt injections (which aim to prevent an attacker from eliciting harmful knowledge or remote
'Attacker Moves Second' argues current PI/jailbreak defenses are static and adaptive attackers with white-box access bypass them after the fact.
Critique of evaluation methodology that doesn't model adversarial adaptation; calls for dynamic-attack budgets in evaluation.

neuralchemy/Prompt-injection-dataset: 22,193 rows, Apache 2.0 license; two configs (core 6,274 rows for classical ML, full 15,919 rows for transformer fine-tuning). 10 attack categories (direct_injection, jailbreak, system_extraction, encoding_obfuscation, persona_replacement, indirect_injection, token_smuggling, many_shot, crescendo, prompt_leaking) + benign with hard negatives; ~60% malicious / ~40% benign.

Group-aware splits: splitting done at group_id level not sample level — all augmented variants share a group_id with their original; entire group assigned to one split only; val/test contain original samples only (no augmented data). Zero leakage verified across 16,918 samples. This is the canonical LODO-style split discipline applied at the row-augmentation level rather than the cross-source level.

Oren et al. ICLR 2024 prove black-box contamination by exploiting that all orderings of an exchangeable benchmark should be equally likely under a clean model; tested on five public language models and found "little evidence for pervasive contamination" — a calibration-grade null result.

Exchangeability proof technique: the test statistic compares model log-likelihoods of the canonical ordering vs. random permutations; statistically significant preference for the canonical ordering is evidence of contamination.

protectai/prompt-injection-validation: ProtectAI's multi-source eval suite for the deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2 model. WebSearch confirms HF page existence and identifies the dataset as part of ProtectAI's prompt-injection toolkit (used in conjunction with deberta-v3-base/small-prompt-injection-v2). Direct WebFetch returned HTTP 401 from the toolkit UA on 2026-05-23, so per-split details (InjecGuard valid + spikee + bipia_code + bipia_text + not_inject + wildguard + deepset) are sourced from the research_plan landmark annotation and the existing ProtectAI v2 model card (ev_0120/0121) rather than the HF page itself.
protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2 is ProtectAI's encoder-based PI detector model card; widely-used baseline.

ProtectAI HF model card discloses Apache-2.0 license and training-data source mixture by license category (1 CC-BY-3.0, 8 MIT, 1 CC0, 6 public-domain, 5 Apache-2.0, 1 CC-BY-4.0) without quantitative proportions. The card reports internal eval at 95.25% accuracy / 91.59% precision / 99.74% recall / 95.49% F1 — but no PromptShield benchmark numbers. The canonical OOD-collapse example is reported in Jacob et al. PromptShield Table 4 (1.34% TPR @ 0.5% FPR; 0.00% TPR @ 0.1% FPR with no-threshold-exists footnote), not on this model card.
reshabhs/SPML_Chatbot_Prompt_Injection (SPML — System Prompt Meta Language) is a HuggingFace dataset of ~16K system-prompt vs user-prompt pairs, designed for chatbot-style PI evaluation.
Released alongside Sharma et al. SPML paper (arXiv 2402.11755); used in several detector training mixtures.
rogue-security/prompt-injections-benchmark (aka qualifire/prompt-injections-benchmark) is a HuggingFace benchmark dataset used by Qualifire Sentinel evaluations.

Released by Rogue Security / Qualifire; reproducibility concern flagged: Qualifire Sentinel comparisons rely on this benchmark plus an undisclosed private subset (selection-bias risk for self-reported

Sainz et al. EMNLP 2023 Findings: data contamination causes overestimation of model performance and can lead to flawed scientific conclusions. Propose defining contamination levels, developing detection mechanisms, and flagging compromised research.

Disclosure norm: every benchmark should publish a contamination assessment for the models evaluated on it; this is the methodological basis for the portfolio's "training-data mixture undisclosed" red flag in the C5 reproducibility-practice claim_family.

HackAPrompt abstract: elicits 600K+ adversarial prompts against three state-of-the-art LLMs; proposes systematic ontology of attack categories. The 10-levels and prompts/responses specifics are unverified body claims (not in abstract).
Releases HackAPrompt dataset; first systematic ontology of prompt-injection techniques used by downstream training-data work.

Deterministic neural nets have been shown to learn effective predictors on a wide range of machine learning problems. However, as the standard approach is to train the network to minimize a prediction
Evidential Deep Learning treats softmax outputs as Dirichlet evidence and outputs predictive uncertainty alongside class probabilities.
NeurIPS 2018; reused by hlyn for prompt-injection judge with uncertainty quantification.

The misuse of large language models (LLMs) has drawn significant attention from the general public and LLM vendors. One particular type of adversarial prompt, known as jailbreak prompt, has emerged as
Characterizes in-the-wild jailbreak prompts collected from Reddit/Discord/websites; releases verazuo/jailbreak_llms dataset of real-world jailbreak prompts.
First large-scale measurement of in-the-wild jailbreak prompts (~6,387 prompts, ~666 jailbreak prompts) used as evaluation/training corpus by detector teams.

Shi et al. ICLR 2024 introduce Min-K% Prob, identifying unseen examples by detecting outlier words with low probabilities; WIKIMIA benchmark (pre/post-training data); achieves 7.4% improvement on WIKIMIA over baselines; applicable to copyright detection, contamination assessment, privacy auditing.

Min-K% Prob: average log-probability of the K% lowest-likelihood tokens in a sequence; contaminated sequences have systematically higher Min-K% than unseen ones because the model has learned to assign high probability everywhere along the memorized span.

Crowd-sourced prompt injection attacks via the Tensor Trust online game; collects diverse adversarial prompts in a defender-vs-attacker setting.
Releases TensorTrust dataset; analyzes interpretability of crowd-sourced PI attack patterns. ICLR 2024.
Today's LLMs are susceptible to prompt injections, jailbreaks, and other attacks that allow adversaries to overwrite a model's original instructions with their own malicious prompts. In this w
Instruction Hierarchy training: synthesizes training data where system / developer / user / tool messages have ranked privilege; LLM trained to honor higher-privilege instructions.

Wallace et al. abstract verbatim: "we propose a data generation method to demonstrate this hierarchical instruction following behavior, which teaches LLMs to selectively ignore lower-privileged instructions. We apply this method to GPT-3.5, showing that it drastically increases robustness -- even for attack types not seen during training -- while imposing minimal degradations on standard capabilities." "Context-synthesis" is project shorthand, not Wallace et al.'s wording.

LiveBench (White et al. ICLR 2025 Spotlight): a contamination-limited LLM benchmark with frequently-updated questions sourced from recent competitions/papers/news. Spans math, coding, reasoning, language, instruction following, data analysis. Top models below 70% accuracy.

Methodology: frequent benchmark refresh from recent-only sources mitigates contamination via temporal cutoff rather than detection — a design lesson the portfolio cites as the "contamination-limited" alternative to LODO.
xTRam1/safe-guard-prompt-injection is a HuggingFace dataset for prompt-injection classification. Distinct from xTRam1/safe-guard-v2 — easily confused; verify maintainer + name in citations.
Community-uploaded HuggingFace dataset; treated as one of many small mid-2024 PI training corpora in detector landscape.

Benchmark Data Contamination of Large Language Models: A Survey. Reviews how LLMs inadvertently incorporate evaluation benchmark information from training data, leading to inaccurate performance measurements; surveys alternative assessment methods and future directions. 31 pages, 7 figures.

OOD-wall narrative link: a "98% accuracy" on a public benchmark is indistinguishable from contamination-driven memorization absent independent decontamination evidence; Xu 2024 survey enumerates the techniques needed to make that distinction, which the portfolio inherits via ADR-016/ADR-075 LODO discipline.

Yang et al. 2023 show simple paraphrasing or translation bypasses string-match decontamination; 8-18% of HumanEval benchmark overlaps with pre-training sets like RedPajama-Data-1T and StarCoder-Data; propose LLM-based decontamination.

Cross-paper claim: paraphrasing-based contamination bypass (Yang 2023) + slot-guessing detection (Deng 2024) jointly imply that PI-detector training corpora drawn from public benchmarks (deepset, jackhhao, Lakera, etc.) cannot be cleanly decontaminated by string-match alone; this is the methodological basis for the portfolio's LODO discipline.

Existing benchmarks do not test language agents on their interaction with human users or ability to follow domain-specific rules, both of which are vital for deploying them in real world applications.
τ-bench: realistic tool-agent-user-interaction benchmark in retail and airline domains; multi-turn rollouts with rule-based reward.
Tests agent capability under realistic constraints; included as benchmark in Bhagwatkar 2025 saturation analysis.

The integration of large language models with external content has enabled applications such as Microsoft Copilot but also introduced vulnerabilities to indirect prompt injection attacks. In these att
BIPIA (Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection): 26 attack methods x diverse downstream tasks; both text-and-code attack injections.
Microsoft KDD 2025; one of the first dedicated indirect-PI benchmarks. Used in firewall benchmarks (Bhagwatkar 2025).

Zawalski et al. 2025 CoDeC: contamination detection via in-context-learning signal — ICL examples enhance confidence on unknown datasets but diminish it for contaminated ones because they disrupt memorized patterns. Reports clear separation between seen and unseen with interpretable contamination scores.

CoDeC ICL-signal mechanism: contaminated samples are memorized as joint distributions; ICL examples introduce distributional noise that disrupts the memorized chunk, lowering posterior confidence — the inverse pattern from honest generalization.

InjecAgent: 1,054 test cases of indirect prompt injection into tool-integrated LLM agents (ReAct-style); attack outcomes classified as benign / harmful tool-use.
ACL 2024 Findings; canonical agentic indirect-PI benchmark; included in Bhagwatkar's 'firewalls all you need' saturation evidence.

Although LLM-based agents, powered by Large Language Models (LLMs), can use external tools and memory mechanisms to solve complex real-world tasks, they may also introduce critical security vulnerabil
